skill.name: sop-product-launch
skill.description: A 10-week product launch SOP that coordinates research, product, engineering, marketing, sales, support, and post-launch monitoring work.
skill.summary: Coordinate a full product launch with phased workflows, agent roles, deliverables, and launch metrics.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: The static Ruby or shell backtick findings are false positives caused by Markdown JavaScript examples and Task prompt template literals. I found no prompt injection attempt, but the SOP has a high-confidence semantic risk because it asks agents to perform production deployment, app submission, and paid marketing without explicit approval gates.

remediation.issue: Live deployment and paid campaign steps lack explicit approval gates.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before production deployment, app store submission, ad spend, email sends, PR outreach, CRM changes, or support system changes.

remediation.issue: Executable-looking Task examples may encourage autonomous execution.
remediation.suggestion: Add a dry-run planning mode and instruct agents to produce plans for review before using tools that affect external systems.

remediation.issue: Markdown code examples trigger scanner noise.
remediation.suggestion: Consider labeling examples as pseudocode or adding safety comments that no shell command execution is intended.

content.value_statement: Product launches need coordinated research, development, marketing, sales, and support work. This skill provides a 10-week SOP with agent assignments, deliverables, and metrics.
actual_capabilities: Breaks a launch plan into five phases across a 10-week timeline.
Assigns work across research, product, engineering, marketing, sales, support, and operations roles.
Shows sequential and parallel Task workflows with shared memory namespaces.
Defines deliverables for strategy, development, launch assets, support resources, and monitoring.
Lists technical, business, marketing, and support success metrics.
Includes a usage pattern for invoking the SOP from Claude Code.
limitations: It does not execute launch work by itself without a compatible agent environment.
It assumes Task, memory, and optional swarm tools are available.
Example namespaces and timelines need adaptation for each organization.
It does not replace legal, compliance, budget, or executive approval.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Product Launch
use_cases.description: Convert a high-level product idea into phased workstreams, deliverables, and measurable launch goals.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Cross-Functional Teams
use_cases.description: Align engineering, marketing, sales, support, and operations around a shared launch sequence.

use_cases.title: Standardize Launch Operations
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable SOP for launch execution, monitoring, and weekly post-launch optimization.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Launch Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single product launch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the product launch SOP to outline a 10-week launch plan for [product]. Include phases, owners, deliverables, and success metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt the Timeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for a different launch window.
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the SOP for a [number]-week launch timeline. Keep the same workstreams, but adjust sequencing, dependencies, and approval checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Build Department Workstreams
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the SOP to create separate workstreams for product, engineering, marketing, sales, support, and operations. Include dependencies and handoff points.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Controlled Launch Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the SOP launch plan for execution risk. Identify missing approvals, unsafe automation, budget exposure, and rollback requirements before any live action.

output_examples.input: A product manager asks for a launch plan for a SaaS analytics product.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a phased launch roadmap with research, development, marketing, sales, launch week, and post-launch monitoring tasks.

output_examples.input: A founder needs sales and support readiness before launch.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines sales enablement assets, support documentation, help desk setup, training materials, and escalation procedures.

output_examples.input: An operations lead wants post-launch tracking metrics.
output_examples.output: The skill lists weekly review inputs, performance metrics, marketing metrics, revenue signals, and support quality measures.

best_practices: Customize each agent role, namespace, and deliverable before assigning real work.
Add approval gates before deployment, paid advertising, customer outreach, or store submission.
Use the metrics section to define measurable launch targets before execution begins.
anti_patterns: Do not run the SOP as an unrestricted autonomous launch command.
Do not use the example timelines without validating team capacity and dependencies.
Do not treat generated launch assets as approved legal, compliance, or brand content.

faq.question: What does this skill help coordinate?
faq.answer: It coordinates a full product launch across planning, development, marketing, sales, support, execution, and monitoring.

faq.question: Does it require Claude Code?
faq.answer: It includes Claude Code Task examples, but the SOP can also guide manual planning in compatible tools.

faq.question: Can it run a launch automatically?
faq.answer: It should not run a launch without review. Users should add approvals before any live deployment or external campaign.

faq.question: Which teams benefit most?
faq.answer: Product, engineering, marketing, sales, support, operations, and leadership teams can use the phased structure.

faq.question: What should users customize first?
faq.answer: Users should update the product context, launch dates, agent roles, budgets, legal requirements, and success targets.

faq.question: What outputs should users expect?
faq.answer: Users should expect plans, task assignments, deliverable lists, metrics, and review checkpoints for launch execution.
